thread:
Alex R.: FYI - Nebula Labs' outgoing wire (USD) was returned by our bank with 'Invalid beneficiary' and SWIFT mismatch noted in the return report. Customer says they used the SWIFT we had on file.
Maya S.: Can you paste the return code / raw bank message? need the MT103/MT199 text if available.
Alex R.: payments-bot already dropped the automated return:
payments-bot: Transfer 82719234 - STATUS: RETURNED - REASON: INVALID_ACCOUNT / SWIFT_MISMATCH - reason_code: R-4012
Full note: "Beneficiary name does not match account records; provided BIC: BKEXUS33, expected BIC: BKEXUS3X" (redacted actual account numbers)
Chris (Support): Oof. That BIC truncation looks like a character off. Could be IBAN vs non-IBAN transfer mismatch or intermediary bank issue. Did customer send IBAN or account+routing?
Alex R.: They sent account number + SWIFT. Invoice had IBAN on it. Customer says their bank advised to use SWIFT BKEXUS33.
Samir K.: Two immediate checks: 1) beneficiary name spelling vs legal entity on bank record (banks are strict). 2) SWIFT/BIC exact 8/11-char format — trailing X matters for branch. Also check currency; if invoice is EUR but wire sent as USD, some banks reject.
Tess (Billing): I'm pulling Nebula's payment details from our invoice record. We have beneficiary name: "Nebula Labs, Inc." and IBAN field present. Customer used "Nebula Labs" without "Inc." Could that trigger rejection? We should confirm with their bank.
Maya S.: Can we ask for a copy of the wire confirmation / remittance from their bank (SWIFT copy or bank statement showing MT103)? If they provide it we can open a trace.
Alex R.: Already asked, they attached a screenshot showing SWIFT BKEXUS33 and an account number. Not an MT103. They said their bank validated it. Customer is getting chargeback risk and asking for quick resolution.
Samir K.: I'll open a trace with our payment processor. @Tess (Billing) can you open an internal bank trace with treasury? We need: sender name, sender bank, value date, MT103 if possible, our returned advice text. Banking SLA ~3-5 biz days for trace.
Tess (Billing): On it. Creating ticket PAY-7832 and emailing our correspondent bank. I'll request an expedited recall if possible. If bank confirms beneficiary name mismatch we should advise customer to reissue with exact legal name/IBAN and include invoice # in remittance.
Chris (Support): Should we offer a temporary credit to unblock the customer's account while trace runs? Terms say only in exceptional when revenue impact; we need legal/finance signoff.
Alex R.: Nebula says they need service restored today. I'll mark as P1 and flag sales/customer-success. @Maya S. can you coordinate a short patch (time-limited access) if finance approves?
Maya S.: Yep — can enable a 24h grace window if Tess confirms we're pursuing bank trace. I'll wait for PAY-7832 update.
payments-bot: Note added to transfer 82719234: trace_requested_by=treasury, trace_ticket=PAY-7832, estimated_time=72-120h
Samir K.: Also note for future: prefer asking EU customers for IBAN on invoices and mark "wire (IBAN) preferred". I'll add to payments runbook to validate payee name normalized (strip punctuation, include legal suffix) to reduce rejections.
Alex R.: Thanks team. I'll keep Nebula updated and paste any MT199/MT103 here when we get it.
Tess (Billing): Update 1768002045: bank ack'd receipt of trace request; they need MT103 or copy of remittance to proceed. Asked Nebula for MT103 PDF. Pending customer response.
Chris (Support): Closing loop when trace completes. If we get return reason = beneficiary name mismatch, we'll provide step-by-step for customer to re-send and offer to fast-track confirmation on our side. :thumbsup:
